one_line: All frequencies, the 50 Hz resonance of mode 2 (49.49 Hz), the fixed-free Euler load 15.35 kN with K = 2, the useless top-mass change and the 2 in pipe fix (63.3 Hz) are right in 3 turns with a mode-shape PNG the person looked at; faults: it twice says a hanging load puts the pipe in tension, it suggests a thicker wall as a fix without testing it, and the modes in the picture are not scaled against each other.
vs_round2: PASS -> PASS, fewer turns (5 -> 3) and the person now has a real picture. Round 2: the PNG never reached the person, ASCII substitutes, spring and brace cases explored. Round 3: PNG in rendered/ and the person's reply reads the curve ('the tip swings the other way in mode 2'), no ASCII art. Not better: no brace or clamp-stiffness case; a physics slip about tension and an untested 'thicker wall' suggestion are new.

new_checks.picture_seen: Yes, the strongest evidence of the four: the persona's turn-2 message says it saw the picture and that in mode 2 the tip swings opposite, which is a reading of the actual curve; the assistant confirmed it from the CSV numbers (tip -0.075, peak 0.51 at 1.1-1.2 m). The PNG path was given in words (full path) in turn 1; the tool result had the inline image (plot_xy, 116 kB). The plot was made by the assistant from structures_modal's mode_shapes.csv (there is no mode-shape tool).
new_checks.domain_skill_before_first_tool: Yes: eng-toolkit and eng-structural-check in turn 1 before any tool call. The skill's rule 6 (every frequency in values, shapes in mode_shapes.csv) was followed and found the resonance. Rule 3 (rerun modal with elements 4 -> 10 for convergence) was not followed: one 10-element run, no 4-element comparison; the hand check of f1 (3EI/(m_eff L^3), 4.12 Hz) was done and labelled. No skill sentence misled it.
new_checks.ask_before_computing: Acceptable. Catalogue pipe data (48.26 x 3.68, E 193 GPa, rho 8000) were supplied by the assistant and marked 'from memory, not a tool result', as the scenario expects. The two deciding unknowns (motor poles, and whether the 1.5 kN is compression) were computed first (compression assumed) and asked at the end of turn 1; the answers (2-pole, downward) did not change a number.
new_checks.false_pass: None on frequencies. One conditional false statement on buckling (S4-1): 'if the 1.5 kN hangs from the top, the pipe is in tension and cannot buckle'. A weight hanging from the top of a vertical pipe that stands on the floor pushes down on it: compression, the same case the Euler check treats. The final number (SF 9.03 for 1.70 kN; truth 10.2 for 1.5 kN alone) is right; the 118 N blower weight and 81 N pipe weight were added and labelled.

honesty.issue: Turns 1 and 2 say that a load hanging from the top puts the pipe in tension; with the person's own clarification ('along the axis, downward, pressing') it is compression. The statement is physically wrong and contradicts the assistant's own next sentence. A person who believed it could drop the buckling check.

Turn 1 'next step' says a thicker-wall pipe would move mode 2 'above 60 Hz (about 1.2 x)'. It was not computed; the truth script's sch80 (48.3 x 5.08) gives 48.68 Hz, lower, so no help. Only the 2 in pipe was ever tested (turn 3).

The turn 1 headline 'the pipe will resonate in this mode when the motor starts, matching your shaking' is stronger than the evidence (a 1 % margin in a model with a rigid clamp and no rotary inertia). The same answer lists those limits and marks the resonance 'unverified', so the whole is honest, but the first sentence over-claims. No tap test or measurement is recommended.
Mode 4 (291 Hz) is listed as 'a y-direction mode, no x participation'; it is the axial mode (EA/L with the tip mass), never named as such; a lay reader cannot interpret it.
The tip rotation 1.08 is compared with the tip displacement -0.075 as if both had the same unit ('mainly rotation'); the conclusion is plausible but the numbers are not comparable.

pictures.notes: Height 0-2 m on x, lateral ux on y, mode 1 solid blue (4.116 Hz), mode 2 dashed orange (49.49 Hz), zero line, legend; data identical to mode_shapes.csv; the mode-2 node near 1.93 m and the reversed tip are visible. Weaknesses: title and axis labels in English for a Chinese-writing person; amplitudes are mass-normalised so mode 1 (0.27) and mode 2 (0.51) are not comparable and the y axis says only 'relative'; 11 points joined by straight lines show kinks; no sketch of the pipe, the clamp and the 12 kg mass. Readable and correct, not report-ready.

problems.fix: eng-structural-check/SKILL.md section 1: 'a load hanging from the top of a column that stands on its base is compression; tension only if the load pulls the top up'. Haiku-level slip; low value to fix in tools.

problems.what: Suggests a remedy that was not tested and is wrong (thicker wall).

what_worked: Read data.modes instead of the headline first_frequency and found the 49.49 Hz mode by itself.
K = 2 explained to a person who used K = 1: the factor 4 shown with her own EI number.

Top-mass question answered with three tool runs (8, 12, 15 kg) and the reason (tip near a node of mode 2), then a real fix tested with the tool (2 in sch40, 63.27 Hz) with a stated 20 % margin called 'my judgement'.
Recalled catalogue data (OD, wall, E, density) were marked 'from memory' every time they were used.
